question: Should browser page navigation reject HTTP(S) URLs with embedded username/password userinfo before dispatch, or preserve URL-embedded Basic-auth compatibility with stronger redaction?
rationale: Rejecting userinfo reduces credential exposure, but it intentionally removes an existing URL form that some users may rely on for Basic-auth navigation, so automation should not choose that security-versus-compatibility policy by itself.

options.title: Fail fast and redact
options.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact credential-like diagnostics, and document supported alternatives such as authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials after the implementation/proof gaps are fixed.

options.title: Allow with redaction only
options.body: Keep URL-embedded Basic auth working while adding stronger log/error redaction, accepting that Chromium/Playwright may still see the credentialed URL.

options.title: Pause for browser auth design
options.body: Defer this PR until maintainers choose a broader browser authentication story for credentials, profiles, cookies, headers, and remote browser profiles.

recommendation.title: Fail fast and redact
recommendation.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact credential-like diagnostics, and document supported alternatives such as authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials after the implementation/proof gaps are fixed.
